chunks: And from him, from a man who bequeathed to a man that he should give his relatives from his estate such and such a Jarib of food.
So years passed by and there was no surplus in his estate, but rather he needed loans and advances. Is it for him to borrow a loan in advance or not?
So if he profits after that, does he compensate them for what was missed from the past years?
So he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not mind if he gives them or takes, then pays it back.'

key_terms.جَرِيباً: a unit of measurement for area or volume
key_terms.وَالْعِينَةِ: and 'aynah (merchandise sold on credit then bought back for cash)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an executor borrowing money to fulfill a bequest if the estate has no surplus?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the flexibility in fulfilling a bequest of specific quantities (such as food from an estate) when immediate surplus is unavailable, permitting the executor to incur debt (salaf or 'aynah) to meet the obligation. The Imam’s response highlights that the priority is ensuring the beneficiaries receive their due, whether through the executor's personal funds or by deducting from future estate yields, emphasizing practical justice over rigid procedural constraints. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (yusr) in financial obligations, ensuring that bequests are not rendered void by temporary liquidity issues.

en.hubeali: And from him<sup>asws</sup>, about a man who bequeathed to a man that he should give his relatives from his place such a such a ‘Jareyb’ (unit of measurement) of food.

So years passed by and there was no grace in his place, but it was needy for the loans and advances upon the one who had bequeathed to him. Is it for him to borrow a loan in advance or not, so that if they profit after that so he can recompense against them due to what he had given them in the past years?’

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> don’t mind if he gives them or takes but then pays it’. 
P.s. – ‘Al Aynah’ is merchandise sold on credit then bought back for cash at a lower price – see Volume five, Chapter 88)’.
en.sarwar: 24. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith who has narrated the following: “A man made a will to another man to give his relatives from his asset (land) such and such Jarib (a certain unit of measurement) of food.

Many years passed but there was no extra in his asset; instead he needed to borrow and arrange for al-‘Aynah on the beneficiary of the will. Is it necessary to arrange a loan and al- ‘Aynah for the beneficiary so that when in future there is a gain it is compensated for what he borrowed for them during the past years?

He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not mind if he gives them or takes then pays off.’” (al-‘ Aynah: merchandise sold on credit is purchased back for cash at a lower price called ( ‘Aynah), see details in Volume Five, Chapter 88)
